title: H397 STUB: EFS Evolutionary Factor Search on H198 30-Stock Universe
rationale: EFS (arXiv:2507.17211, Luo, Zhang & Liu, July 2025 / newly active 2026) reformulates asset selection as a top-m ranking task where LLM-generated factor expressions are refined by an evolutionary feedback loop (mutation + crossover based on realized IC). Outperforms statistical and optimization baselines especially in larger universes and volatile conditions. Tested on Fama-French benchmark datasets + US50, HSI45, CSI300. H397 tests EFS directly on the H198 30-stock large-cap universe to determine whether evolutionary LLM factor discovery can produce a composite exceeding H395 OOS Sharpe 3.962 (current family champion). Uses existing $OPENAI_API_KEY. The sparse top-m framing matches H395's top-1/top-2 design exactly.
content: h397_status: STUB (2026-07-13) — EFS Evolutionary Factor Search on H198 Universe (arXiv:2507.17211). Luo, Zhang & Liu reformulate asset selection as LLM-generated top-m ranking with evolutionary feedback: mutation and crossover based on realized IC across a test window. Outperforms baselines on FF datasets + US50. H397 design: (1) Seed EFS with H395 Var C formula (0.33×IMOM6 + 0.33×MOM60 + 0.33×LowVol) as starting factor. (2) Evolutionary loop: LLM generates 10-15 mutation candidates per round (e.g., add MOM12, change IMOM window, add realized skew, try momentum-of-vol). (3) Evaluate each candidate's rolling IC on IS 2013-2020. (4) Keep top-3 by IS IC; cross-breed to generate next generation (3-5 rounds). (5) Final OOS backtest on 2021-2026 with gate: OOS Sharpe > 3.962 (H395 Var C) OR novel factor expression not in existing hypothesis log. Gate rationale: evolutionary search should outperform human-designed baseline if it has real discriminative power. Cost: ~$20-35 OpenAI (moderate, ~50-70 factor evaluations). Script: backtesting/daily/run_h397_efs_mining.py (stub). Low risk.
